findings.summary: The omitted-variables-bias formula mislabels the auxiliary slope $\delta_{23}$ as "the correlation"; in Bias = β3×δ₂₃ the second factor is the regression coefficient (slope) of the omitted variable on the included regressor, not the correlation coefficient.
findings.old: where $\beta_3$ is the omitted variable's effect and $\delta_{23}$ is the correlation
findings.new: where $\beta_3$ is the omitted variable's effect and $\delta_{23}$ is the slope from an auxiliary regression of the omitted variable on the included regressor
findings.evidence: Standard OVB result: for true model y=β1+β2 x2+β3 x3+u, regressing y on x2 alone gives plim(b2)=β2+β3·δ where δ is the population slope of x3 on x2. Magnitude of the correlation coefficient ≠ magnitude of the slope, so the multiplicative term in Bias=β3×δ₂₃ must be the slope. Lens A rule: OVB claims are stated in terms of the omitted's effect × its relationship to the included regressor (auxiliary slope).
findings.verify_note: The exact omitted-variables-bias identity Bias = beta3 x delta_{23} uses the auxiliary-regression SLOPE (a regression coefficient), not the correlation coefficient; slope = correlation x (SD_omitted/SD_included), so they differ in magnitude. The delta notation itself denotes a slope. Proposed replacement ('slope from an auxiliary regression of the omitted variable on the included regressor') is the correct definition and matches the chapter's own auxiliary-regression usage. old text matches uniquely at L1526.
